title: Sultana Rolls with Sugar Glaze
description: Warmly spiced, tender sultana rolls portioned into individual buns. Ground allspice and brown sugar provide depth, spreadable butter keeps the crumb soft, and a shiny sugar glaze made with glucose syrup to prevent crystallization is brushed on top after baking.

ingredients.notes: soaked in warm water for 10 minutes, drained and patted dry

method.instruction: Place sultanas in a bowl, cover with warm water and soak for 10 minutes. Drain well and pat dry with paper towel. Set aside.

In a large bowl, combine bread flour, yeast, bread improver, brown sugar, ground allspice, and softened spreadable butter. Add 300 ml of the water. Keep salt on the opposite side of the bowl from the yeast before mixing. Mix until a shaggy dough forms.

Tip out onto a lightly floured bench and knead for 12 minutes until smooth and elastic. In the final 2 to 3 minutes of kneading, fold in the drained sultanas gradually — work them in gently so they stay whole and distribute evenly without tearing the dough.
Shape the dough into a ball, place in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with a damp cloth or plastic wrap, and allow to prove in a warm spot for 1 hour or until doubled in size.

Knock back the dough and divide into 9 equal portions (approximately 125g each). Shape each portion into a smooth round roll and place onto a baking tray lined with baking paper, leaving roughly 2-3cm of space between them. Cover and allow to prove for a further 30 to 45 minutes until risen and touching slightly.
Preheat oven to 190 degrees Celsius fan-forced. Bake the rolls for 15 to 18 minutes until golden brown.

While the rolls are baking, prepare the glaze. In a small saucepan, combine 50 g caster sugar, the remaining 50 ml of water, and 15 g glucose syrup. Heat gently over low heat, stirring continuously until the sugar and syrup are completely dissolved. Bring to a brief boil for 1 minute without stirring, then remove from heat.
Brush the warm sugar glaze generously over the hot rolls immediately as they come out of the oven. Transfer the rolls to a wire rack to cool before serving.

notes.title: Soaking Sultanas
notes.content: Soaking sultanas in warm water before kneading prevents them from absorbing moisture from the dough itself, keeping the final baked rolls soft and tender.
